messages:
Alice Chen: Quick sync — I prototyped a small card for the console that shows an amortized per-call cost after prefetched cache credits are applied. Wanted feedback on two things: 1) how we show sampled telemetry vs full-scan numbers, and 2) whether routing policies should surface a projected delta when you change model variant on the fly.
Samir Patel: Nice. For sampling: show sampled value + confidence interval, and a footnote with sample rate. Don’t pretend it’s exact. :white_check_mark:
Priya Nair: Agree on CI. Also: add a toggle to show raw sample counts so PMs know when numbers are noisy.
Marco Ruiz: For routing preview: we should show "if routed -> projected token cost change" for the last 24h and for a canonical 1k call workload. Otherwise folks misinterpret per-token vs per-invocation.
Alice Chen: Good call. UX idea: mini-sparkline + an overlay that flips to a 1k invocation hypothetical. Keeps the main card compact.
Samir Patel: Implementation note: our current telemetry pipeline down-samples prefetch/cache attribution events aggressively. If we want CI we need to bump retention for the attribution tags or run a background job to rehydrate a denser sample for the card. That will cost infra.
Priya Nair: Can we do a hybrid? Keep lightweight sampling for default, but rehydrate on-demand when a user clicks "Deep sample" (async job + progress spinner).
Marco Ruiz: That matches how we do canary rollups elsewhere. Customers clicking deep sample should be rate-limited. Also we need to show an "expected error" metric when sample size < 500.
Alice Chen: Sounds good. Edge case: cache credits are applied at batch time; per-request accounting can be ambiguous. Proposal: show two columns — "Estimated per-invocation cost (post-credit)" and "Credit attribution method" (e.g., session, prefix, prefetch).
Samir Patel: And add a link to the attribution rules; people keep assuming we split prefetch 50/50 when we use slab amortization.
Priya Nair: API debate: should the internal route-cost-preview API accept a hypothetical routing policy payload and return a simulated delta? Or should the console send simulated requests to the real routing engine?
Marco Ruiz: Simulate. Hitting real routing could alter caches and pollute metrics. Simulation is safer — we have the model of hotpath frequency + slab credits.
Samir Patel: Implementation sketch: create /internal/cost_preview POST {policy, time_range, sample_seed} -> returns {projected_delta, sample_rate_used, ci_low, ci_high, underlying_assumptions}. Keep it internal-only and rate-limited.
Priya Nair: +1 but include a user-visible reason code when assumptions are weak (e.g., "low sample support", "prefetch dominated").
ops-bot: Reminder: cost_preview API is currently rate-limited to 10/min for non-admins in staging.
Alice Chen: Final UX asks: (a) compact card with sparkline + 1k-call hypothetical switch, (b) deep-sample flow with progress + estimate of extra compute cost, (c) simulated routing preview button that calls internal API and surfaces assumptions.
Marco Ruiz: I'll own the routing-preview API PR. Samir, can you estimate the extra retention cost for rehydration?
Samir Patel: I'll throw numbers in a follow-up tomorrow — rough estimate now: ~2-4% extra storage for the attribution tag index if we keep 7d instead of 1d sampling, plus ephemeral compute for rehydrate jobs.
Priya Nair: I'll draft the console copy for the confidence UI and the assumptions panel.
Alice Chen: Great — thanks team. If nobody objects, I'll add the card prototype to the design board and tag infra + API owners. :rocket:
Marco Ruiz: No objections from me.
Samir Patel: Fine by infra.
Priya Nair: LGTM.
Alice Chen: Closing thread — will post mockups once they're in Figma.
